rows.selection_reason: No prior experiments exist, so the first step is to establish a baseline. This experiment tests RNA-only modeling with PCA encoding and singleprofile, isolating the impact of the RNA modality and basic encoding. It clarifies whether RNA data alone can achieve reasonable performance, providing foundational evidence for comparing multimodal approaches later.

The existing evidence shows that singleprofile RNA-only models with PCA encoding achieve moderate accuracy (0.4849). This experiment tests the impact of multiprofile setting with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile structure while keeping RNA encoder and image encoder unchanged. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether multiprofile configurations improve performance, which is a critical design choice with potential for significant gains.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile models. This experiment tests whether adding image data (resnet50) and concat fusion improves performance on multiprofile data, isolating the effect of multimodal integration. It builds on the successful multiprofile setting while introducing a key design choice (image modality) to determine if multimodal approaches yield gains.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and resnet50 image encoders (e.g., config_018) outperform RNA-only or image-only baselines. This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion (a key design choice in multimodal models) improves performance, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It builds on the strong evidence for multimodal/multiprofile setups while exploring a critical component of model architecture.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models (e.g., config_019) outperform RNA-only models, and weighted fusion (config_019) is better than concat. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (used in config_019) with transformer aggregation (a more complex method) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation strategy. It builds on the current best configuration while exploring a key design choice with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a more complex image encoder) while keeping other parameters fixed. It isolates the impact of image encoder architecture, which is critical for multimodal performance, and could reveal if ViT outperforms ResNet50 in this domain.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a different representation method) while keeping other parameters the same isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice. This is critical for understanding if representation quality is a key factor, and whether scvi_n200 could further improve performance.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder (config_031) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l image encoder while keeping scvi_n200 RNA encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (same as config_031). This isolates the impact of the image encoder choice, which is critical for multimodal performance. It balances exploitation (building on the successful scvi_n200 RNA encoder) and exploration (testing a stronger image encoder).

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, multiprofile, and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.7062). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation (while keeping other parameters the same) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, a key design choice, and explores whether more complex aggregation could enhance results without changing other critical components.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (config_051) while keeping other components identical isolates the impact of the RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of a new RNA encoder, avoiding redundant changes and focusing on a critical design decision.
